comparator.name: Science for Sustainable Societies
comparator.academicYear: Current 2026–27 OER and programme pages, checked 2026-09-27; the adopted 2025–26 OER supplies the last published component-level EC table
comparator.route: Ordinary 180-EC English-taught full-time BSc; all compulsory components plus the programme’s 30-EC third-year minor/elective/exchange space
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Science OER appendix confirms the BSc title, interdisciplinary natural- and social-science objective, English language, progression rules and named prerequisites: second-year entry after 45 first-year EC; Systems Modelling after Mathematics for Sustainability and/or Programming in Python; and the Sustainable Societies Project and Thesis Research Project after the first year plus 45 second-year EC including Research Design in Practice. Leiden’s current programme pages and 2026/27 curriculum image continue the same three-year integrated structure. The adopted 2025–26 OER is used only for the detailed credit reconstruction because it is the last official source in this evidence set that prints every named component and EC value. It totals 60 EC in each year: 60 EC foundations; 60 EC integrated thematic and methods work; and 30 EC open minor/elective/exchange space plus an 11-EC Sustainable Societies Project, 18-EC thesis and 1-EC Learning My Way unit. Repeated 1-EC Learning My Way units are retained separately rather than collapsed.

core: Integrated natural-science understanding of climate, Earth systems, ecology and biodiversity
Social and behavioural analysis of human–environment relationships
Governance, policy and socially effective sustainability transitions
Quantitative, computational, spatial and interdisciplinary research methods
adjacent: Pollution, resource use, industrial ecology and energy transitions
questions: How can spatial evidence and natural-science models guide socially workable climate adaptation?
Which governance and economic choices support fair resource and energy transitions?

alternatives.label: Integrated sustainability science
alternatives.concept: Integrates Earth systems, climate, ecology and biodiversity with economics, environmental justice and sustainability governance. Statistics, spatial data and a partner-facing sustainability research project connect natural evidence to societal decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule deliberately spans natural systems, social and economic analysis, policy, quantitative methods and applied sustainability research.
progression: Sustainability, Earth-system, economics and methods foundations precede GIS, hydrology, upper-level environmental science, econometrics and the sustainability research project; prerequisites and term offerings pass.

alternatives.label: Climate resilience and spatial environmental data
alternatives.concept: Focuses on climate hazards, Earth systems, soils and aquifers, delta water management and nature-based adaptation. GIS, satellite data, machine learning and public economics support evidence-based choices about resilient communities.
alternatives.labelReason: The scheduled courses explicitly develop climate risk, water and soils, Earth observation, modelling, data analysis and public choices about adaptation.
progression: Earth and sustainability gateways precede Earth-system modelling, GIS, water and soil analysis; upper-level project, data and policy courses follow their applicable gateways.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the integrated route, this schedule adds Earth-system modelling, machine learning, renewable-system design and public economics while dropping advanced mathematics, microeconomics, environmental justice and one governance course. Its organising question is spatial climate resilience.

alternatives.label: Resources, energy and sustainability policy
alternatives.concept: Links resource geoscience, ecological systems, circular material flows and renewable-system design to economic incentives, externalities, governance and behaviour. It asks how policy and market choices can produce fair resource and energy transitions.
alternatives.labelReason: Resource geoscience, energy design, economics, governance and behavioural choice form the scheduled focus.
progression: Economics and sustainability foundations come before upper-level public economics, resource research, econometrics and renewable-system design; gate and methods prerequisites are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces flood-hazard, aquifer and water-management depth with ecosystems, macroeconomic conditions, public economics, energy design and behavioural choices. It therefore changes both the environmental subject and the policy question.

candidates.label: Climate resilience and spatial environmental data

routeSelection.route: Ordinary 180-EC English-taught full-time BSc; all compulsory components plus the programme’s 30-EC third-year minor/elective/exchange space
routeSelection.basis: The official programme has no named track or specialisation to choose. The reconstruction therefore uses every compulsory component and preserves the full 30-EC open third-year space without filling it to improve UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three evidence-backed UCR programmes are feasible and pairwise distinct by at least four courses: integrated sustainability science; climate resilience with spatial environmental data; and resources, energy and sustainability policy. Remaining interest rows elaborate examples, methods and outcomes rather than a fourth coherent direction.

blocks: Earth systems, ecology, climate and field evidence

Both introduce ecology and biodiversity in the context of sustainability.
Both introduce interacting Earth systems and human pressures.
Both address climate change and societal consequences; UCR emphasizes physical and sustainability dimensions.
Both analyse ecosystems and biodiversity; UCR does not reproduce the Leiden livelihoods module.
Both use models of interacting environmental systems.
Both develop field-based environmental evidence, though UCR focuses on soils and aquifers.
Both introduce governance choices for sustainability.
Both examine social interpretations of environmental change; UCR emphasizes movements and environmental justice rather than anthropology.
Both examine behaviour and decisions; UCR uses microeconomic rather than environmental-psychology framing.
Both examine relations among science, technology and societal transitions.
Both provide foundations for socio-economic policy evaluation.
Both study political and stakeholder choices in sustainability; UCR is not a dedicated food-systems course.
Both address pollution, material flows and power; UCR focuses on circular delta systems.
Both consider responsible innovation for sustainability; UCR focuses on renewable-system design.
Methods, projects and open programme space
Both support reflection and academic development, but Leiden’s Learning My Way is programme-specific.
Both provide mathematical foundations for quantitative sustainability work.
Both teach social-science research design and statistics.
Both introduce programming and data analysis; UCR is not sustainability-specific.
Both design and conduct interdisciplinary sustainability research; UCR’s partner project is a separate course.
Programme-specific second-year Learning My Way unit.

notes.text: Leiden’s BSc integrates named natural- and social-science modules, compulsory field and project work, an 18-EC thesis and 30 EC of open space. UCR offers substantial related coursework and three coherent schedules, but it does not reproduce Leiden’s specified anthropology, integrated field module, 11-EC project or compulsory thesis; pairings indicate intellectual overlap rather than transfer equivalence.
